title: A long walk sweep does not cost a task its runner
goal: Two of the five runner failures in the last day were the same thing: a task kicked off the full walk sweep, which takes about forty minutes, and the runner was killed waiting for it at ten. Each one cost a task in the focus a whole cycle before it was picked up again and finished. Give a runner a way to run the sweep that survives, or a rule not to start one it cannot wait for.
notes:
Design review 2026-09-08, from queue/history.jsonl. Two runner_failed entries in 24 hours are this: with-the-grid-off-only-the-grid-switch-is-on-the at 2026-09-07T16:22, whose note begins "The full walk sweep is still running (it re-runs all 253 walks)", and a-marquee-keeps-the-layer-you-picked-and-delete at 2026-09-08T00:03 with "Background tasks still running after 600s; terminating. Set CLAUDE_CODE_PRINT_BG_WAIT_CEILING_MS=0 to wait indefinitely." Both tasks completed later, so this costs time rather than work. The other three failures in the same window were network errors and are not this.

It is filed at p3 because the loop is a next epic, not the focus, but it protects focus throughput directly: both tasks it cost were ui-building work. a-full-walk-run-finishes-in-an-hour-not-four already cut the sweep from about 60 to 40 minutes, which is still four times the ceiling, so the answer is how it is run, not how fast it is.
acceptance: A runner that needs the whole walk sweep has one documented way to get it that does not end with the runner being terminated
The runner brief says which check to use when: one walk while building, the sweep only when something asks for it
The two failure notes from 2026-09-07 and 2026-09-08 are named in the writeup so a reader can see the real case
Nothing about how a single walk is run changes
